types.name: Painters
types.who: Studio painters selling through galleries, open studios, commissions and prints.
types.firstHire: An inventory and consignment agent. Most painters can't say where every canvas is today or which gallery owes them money.

ideas.title: Inventory with provenance
ideas.text: Logs each finished work from a phone photo: size, medium, date, location, price. Keeps exhibition and sale history attached for the certificate of authenticity.

ideas.title: Consignment tracker
ideas.text: Knows which galleries hold which canvases, the split on each, and when each consignment term ends. Chases payment for reported sales and requests unsold work back on schedule.

ideas.title: Open call scout
ideas.text: Reads CaFÉ, Submittable and arts council listings each week, filters by medium, entry fee and eligibility, and drafts the application to the exact image and statement specs.

ideas.title: Collector memory
ideas.text: Remembers who bought what, who lingered at a piece during an opening, and who collects a series. Drafts a personal note when new work in that series leaves the easel.

ideas.title: Commission intake
ideas.text: Handles portrait and mural inquiries: size, deadline, deposit, progress-photo approvals, and a contract that says who holds reproduction rights.

ideas.title: Print editions
ideas.text: Runs a giclée program with the print studio: edition size, numbering, proof approvals and fulfillment. Closes the listing the moment an edition sells out.

ideas.title: Statements in every length
ideas.text: Keeps a 50, 150 and 500 word artist statement in your voice and adapts one to each show, grant or press request.

ideas.title: Shipping and crating
ideas.text: Gets art-shipper quotes, picks a crate or soft pack by value, buys fine-art transit insurance and tracks delivery to the gallery.

ideas.title: Light-hours guard
ideas.text: Blocks your best natural-light hours for painting and pushes every call and errand into one admin afternoon.

types.name: Illustrators & comic artists
types.who: Editorial, publishing and commercial illustrators, plus webcomic and graphic novel creators.
types.firstHire: A contract and licensing reviewer. Illustrators lose more money to bad usage terms than to slow clients.

ideas.title: Contract redlines
ideas.text: Reads every publisher and agency contract for work-for-hire language, all-rights grabs, AI training clauses and missing kill fees, then proposes edits based on your past deals.

ideas.title: Usage-based quotes
ideas.text: Prices a job by territory, term, media and print run using your own history and Graphic Artists Guild ranges, so a national campaign never gets an editorial spot fee.

ideas.title: Revision round counter
ideas.text: Tracks rounds against the contract, flags the round that crosses the limit, and drafts a friendly change order before you start it.

ideas.title: Convention circuit
ideas.text: Applies for artist alley tables, books travel, plans print and sticker stock from last year's sales at that show, and reconciles the card reader report afterward.

ideas.title: Page buffer watch
ideas.text: Keeps count of finished webcomic pages, warns when the buffer drops under two weeks, and posts updates to Webtoon, Tapas and Patreon on schedule.

ideas.title: Art theft sweep
ideas.text: Reverse-image searches print-on-demand shops and social accounts for your work and files takedown notices.

ideas.title: Crowdfunding back end
ideas.text: Runs a Kickstarter book campaign: reward tiers, backer updates, pledge manager surveys, printer quotes, freight, and the shipping spreadsheet.

ideas.title: Portfolio by market
ideas.text: Each quarter picks your strongest new pieces and builds separate portfolios for children's publishing, editorial and licensing clients.

types.name: Sculptors & ceramicists
types.who: Fine art sculptors working with foundries and fabricators, and studio potters selling functional work.
types.firstHire: A fabrication coordinator. A bronze moves through six vendors and a dozen approvals before it's finished.

ideas.title: Foundry tracker
ideas.text: Follows a bronze through mold, wax, casting, chasing and patina, logs cost at each stage, and schedules your approval visits.

ideas.title: Kiln and glaze log
ideas.text: Records firing schedules, cone, atmosphere and glaze recipes with photos of the results, so a glaze that worked last spring can be repeated.

ideas.title: Public art RFQs
ideas.text: Watches percent-for-art programs and city calls, drafts the qualifications packet, and builds a budget with engineering, permits and installation lines.

ideas.title: Cast and edition records
ideas.text: Keeps the edition count, cast number and foundry mark for every piece, which collectors and appraisers will ask for later.

ideas.title: Install logistics
ideas.text: Coordinates riggers, art handlers, site permits and certificates of insurance for a large installation.

ideas.title: Shop drop after the kiln
ideas.text: Turns a kiln unload into a shop update: listing photos, descriptions and prices, an email to the list, and breakage-proof packing rules for shipping.

ideas.title: Materials reorder
ideas.text: Reorders clay, glaze chemicals, armature and welding supplies before you run out, comparing supplier prices and lead times.

ideas.title: Body and dust check
ideas.text: Tracks hours at the wheel or grinder, reminds you to rest your wrists, and tracks respirator cartridge replacement.

types.name: Photographers
types.who: Wedding, portrait, commercial and fine art photographers.
types.firstHire: A client pipeline agent. The inquiry that waits a day goes to the photographer who replied in ten minutes.

ideas.title: Inquiry to booking
ideas.text: Answers inquiries within minutes with availability and packages, then sends the contract and retainer invoice and holds the date.

ideas.title: Timeline and shot list
ideas.text: Builds the shoot timeline around sunset time and travel between locations, with the family formals list and the second shooter's schedule.

ideas.title: First-pass cull
ideas.text: Removes closed eyes, missed focus and near-duplicates from 3,000 frames so you start editing from the keepers, with hero candidates flagged.

ideas.title: Releases on file
ideas.text: Collects model and property releases before the shoot and attaches them to the images, so commercial and stock licensing stays possible.

ideas.title: Unlicensed use recovery
ideas.text: Finds your images used without a license on the web, confirms the use is commercial, and sends a retroactive license invoice.

ideas.title: Stock submissions
ideas.text: Keywords and submits outtakes to stock agencies, tracks which subjects sell, and suggests what to shoot next.

ideas.title: Album and print sales
ideas.text: Follows up after gallery delivery on album selections and print orders, which is where most wedding upsell revenue gets left behind.

ideas.title: Off-season plan
ideas.text: Each January plans mini-sessions, referral outreach and vendor networking so the slow months don't become anxious months.

types.name: Performing musicians & bands
types.who: Touring and gigging artists, bands and solo performers.
types.firstHire: A tour manager agent. One mistake on a settlement sheet can wipe out a week of profit.

ideas.title: Tour routing
ideas.text: Routes a run of dates by drive time, radius clauses and past ticket sales per market, drafts pitches to talent buyers and tracks holds.

ideas.title: Advance and settlement
ideas.text: Advances each show (load-in, backline, hospitality, guest list), then checks the settlement against the deal so a guarantee-versus-door split is calculated right.

ideas.title: Merch counts
ideas.text: Counts merch in and out each night, reorders sizes that sell out before the next market, and reconciles cash and card by city.

ideas.title: Release campaign
ideas.text: Plans a single's rollout: Spotify editorial pitch at least seven days before release, pre-saves, content calendar and curator outreach.

ideas.title: Royalty registrations
ideas.text: Registers every song with your PRO, The MLC and SoundExchange and assigns ISRCs, so streams and radio plays don't go unclaimed.

ideas.title: Band and crew pay
ideas.text: Pays members and crew per show from the split sheet and tracks who fronted the van rental and the strings.

ideas.title: Fans near the next show
ideas.text: Collects emails at shows and announces new dates to fans within driving distance of each city.

ideas.title: Recovery on the road
ideas.text: Plans sleep windows, vocal rest days and real meals into the drive schedule, and pushes back on a routing that leaves no rest.

ideas.title: Press kit upkeep
ideas.text: Keeps the EPK current with fresh numbers, press quotes, photos and live video, ready when a buyer or festival asks.

types.name: Composers & producers
types.who: Songwriters, beatmakers, film and game composers, and catalog owners.
types.firstHire: A sync pitcher with perfect metadata. Music supervisors search by tags, and a track with blank fields never comes up.

ideas.title: Sync pitching
ideas.text: Reads music supervisor briefs, finds matching tracks in your catalog by mood, tempo and lyric theme, prepares instrumentals and stems, and sends the pitch.

ideas.title: Metadata cleanup
ideas.text: Fills writers, publishers, splits, ISWC, ISRC, BPM, key and mood tags across the catalog and embeds your contact in every file.

ideas.title: Cue sheet follow-through
ideas.text: Confirms a cue sheet was filed for every placement and checks PRO statements for performances that never paid.

ideas.title: Split sheets signed
ideas.text: Sends split sheets to every collaborator the day of the session, before memories of who wrote the hook start to differ.

ideas.title: Sample clearance
ideas.text: Identifies the samples in a track, finds the master and publishing owners, and requests clearance quotes before release.

ideas.title: Score revisions
ideas.text: Tracks picture locks and cue revisions on a film or game, manages versions, and delivers stems to the exact sample rate and naming spec.

ideas.title: Beat license terms
ideas.text: Tracks lease versus exclusive terms for every beat sold, and flags a lease that has passed its stream cap so you can upsell it.

ideas.title: Royalty audit
ideas.text: Reconciles distributor, PRO, MLC and SoundExchange statements each quarter and flags any song whose income dropped without a reason.

types.name: YouTubers & online video creators
types.who: Creators who earn from AdSense, sponsors, memberships, affiliates and their own products.
types.firstHire: A brand deal desk. Sponsor email is the biggest pile of unread money in the business.

ideas.title: Brand deal desk
ideas.text: Triages sponsor email, quarantines fake-sponsor malware lures, quotes from real view data, negotiates within your floor and tracks deliverables through to payment.

ideas.title: Edit review
ideas.text: Watches the editor's cut against the brief and sends timestamped notes on pacing, missing B-roll and a sponsor read shorter than the contract requires.

ideas.title: Packaging lab
ideas.text: Writes title and thumbnail variants, scores them against your channel's history and runs the A/B test.

ideas.title: Comment triage
ideas.text: Surfaces the comments that matter (a superfan, a brand, a customer problem, a threat) and drafts replies to them, signed as the team.

ideas.title: Impersonator sweep
ideas.text: Reports scam accounts that copy your name and avatar in replies, and finds deepfake ads using your likeness.

ideas.title: One video, many formats
ideas.text: Cuts a long video into shorts, a newsletter and posts for each platform, following each one's conventions.

ideas.title: Content ID pre-flight
ideas.text: Checks music and clips before upload for anything likely to draw a claim, and drafts fair-use disputes when a claim is wrong.

ideas.title: Unified P&L
ideas.text: Combines AdSense, memberships, merch, affiliates and sponsor invoices into one ledger and sets aside estimated taxes.

ideas.title: Backlog buffer
ideas.text: Keeps a bank of filmed videos so a sick week or a bad month doesn't break the upload schedule.

types.name: Videographers
types.who: Wedding, event and commercial video producers who shoot and edit for clients.
types.firstHire: A production coordinator. Every job is a small production with its own crew, gear, footage and revision rounds.

ideas.title: Quote builder
ideas.text: Prices a job from crew days, gear, edit days and how the client will use it, so a regional TV spot costs more than a social cut.

ideas.title: Pre-production packet
ideas.text: Builds the call sheet, shot list, location notes, weather forecast and permit checklist for each shoot.

ideas.title: Footage safety
ideas.text: Verifies card offloads with checksums, confirms the backups exist in three places, and labels and makes proxies for the editor.

ideas.title: Review rounds
ideas.text: Turns Frame.io comments into a task list for the editor, groups duplicates, and tracks rounds against the contract.

ideas.title: Music license check
ideas.text: Confirms every track in the edit is licensed for the client's use, which matters when a wedding film ends up in a venue's ad.

ideas.title: Freelance crew
ideas.text: Books second shooters and editors, pays them on delivery, and collects W-9s for 1099s at year end.

ideas.title: Repeat business
ideas.text: Turns finished jobs into case studies and reminds past clients about anniversaries, annual events and next year's campaign.

ideas.title: Gear upkeep
ideas.text: Tracks serial numbers, insurance riders, rentals out and returns, and service dates for the camera bodies and drones.

types.name: Independent filmmakers
types.who: Directors and producers making shorts, features and documentaries outside the studio system.
types.firstHire: A line producer agent. Indie films die from schedule and budget chaos more often than from creative failure.

ideas.title: Script breakdown
ideas.text: Breaks the script into cast, props, locations and effects, builds the stripboard and drafts a shooting schedule.

ideas.title: Daily cost report
ideas.text: Tracks spend against budget every shoot day and warns you while there is still time to cut a scene.

ideas.title: Call sheets
ideas.text: Sends the next day's call sheet with weather, parking, nearest hospital and changes highlighted, and confirms everyone read it.

ideas.title: Festival strategy
ideas.text: Picks festivals by premiere rules, fees and deadlines, tracks FilmFreeway submissions, and asks for fee waivers where you qualify.

ideas.title: Grants and incentives
ideas.text: Drafts applications to film funds and labs, and tracks the paperwork for state production incentives.

ideas.title: Clearances and chain of title
ideas.text: Collects every release, location agreement and music license, which E&O insurance and distributors require before they'll touch the film.

ideas.title: Deliverables
ideas.text: Tracks the distributor's deliverables list: DCP, M&E tracks, captions, QC report, key art and stills.

ideas.title: Audience before release
ideas.text: Builds the mailing list and crowdfunding backers into an audience you can bring to screenings and a self-distribution release.

types.name: Writers & authors
types.who: Novelists, nonfiction authors, self-publishers, essayists and freelance journalists.
types.firstHire: A rights and royalties manager. Authors sign away rights they never use and rarely reclaim the ones they could.

ideas.title: Submission tracker
ideas.text: Tracks queries to agents and pieces sent to magazines, each venue's response time and policy on simultaneous submissions.

ideas.title: Royalty reconciliation
ideas.text: Reads KDP, aggregator and publisher statements, checks reserves against returns, and flags anything that doesn't add up.

ideas.title: Rights inventory
ideas.text: Lists foreign, audio, film and translation rights for every book, and tells you when an out-of-print clause lets you take rights back.

ideas.title: Series bible
ideas.text: Keeps characters, timelines, places and invented terms consistent across books, and catches the eye color that changed in book three.

ideas.title: Research librarian
ideas.text: Finds and cites sources for a nonfiction chapter and fact-checks the draft against them.

ideas.title: Launch operations
ideas.text: Runs ARC readers, newsletter swaps, promo bookings and the review requests that make launch week.

ideas.title: Self-publishing production
ideas.text: Coordinates the cover designer, formatting, ISBNs, categories and keywords, and checks every retailer listing is correct.

ideas.title: Word count habit
ideas.text: Logs daily words, protects your writing hours, and stays quiet on the days you need it to.

ideas.title: Pitch desk
ideas.text: For freelancers: tracks editors, their beats and rates, drafts pitches, and chases late payment on published pieces.

types.name: Podcasters
types.who: Interview and narrative shows, independent or network-backed.
types.firstHire: A guest booker. Booking and briefing guests takes more hours than recording them.

ideas.title: Guest booking
ideas.text: Researches guests who fit the show, drafts the outreach, schedules the recording and sends a tech checklist.

ideas.title: Guest brief
ideas.text: Reads the guest's book, past interviews and posts, then suggests questions nobody else has asked them.

ideas.title: Ad inventory
ideas.text: Tracks host-read and dynamic ad slots, confirms each read aired as booked, sends proof of performance and invoices.

ideas.title: Show notes and chapters
ideas.text: Writes show notes, chapter markers, links mentioned and a transcript for every episode.

ideas.title: Clip finder
ideas.text: Finds the strongest moments in each episode and cuts vertical video clips with captions.

ideas.title: Guest releases
ideas.text: Collects a signed release from every guest before the episode publishes.

ideas.title: Listener mail
ideas.text: Sorts listener email and voicemail into questions for a mailbag episode, corrections and guest suggestions.

ideas.title: Download trends
ideas.text: Watches downloads by episode and source and tells you which topics and guests grew the show.

types.name: Designers
types.who: Freelance and studio graphic, brand, web and product designers.
types.firstHire: A scope and invoicing agent. Unbilled scope creep is where design studio margins go.

ideas.title: Scope creep detector
ideas.text: Compares every new request to the statement of work and drafts a change order before the extra work starts.

ideas.title: Proposal builder
ideas.text: Turns a discovery call recording into a proposal with phases, deliverables, timeline and price based on similar past projects.

ideas.title: Feedback merge
ideas.text: Combines feedback from five stakeholders into one list, flags where they contradict each other, and asks the client to decide.

ideas.title: Handoff package
ideas.text: Packages final files, exports, brand guidelines and source files, and checks that fonts and stock images are licensed for the client.

ideas.title: Retainer health
ideas.text: Tracks hours used on each retainer and warns you and the client before the month runs over.

ideas.title: Case studies
ideas.text: Writes a case study from each finished project with the brief, the work and results the client will let you share.

ideas.title: Reference library
ideas.text: Saves and tags inspiration and past work so you can pull every editorial layout with a grid you liked in seconds.

ideas.title: Pipeline outreach
ideas.text: Keeps in touch with past clients and warm leads so a quiet month doesn't become a quiet quarter.

types.name: Makers & craftspeople
types.who: Jewelers, woodworkers, textile artists, candlemakers and other makers selling online and at markets.
types.firstHire: A shop operations agent. Makers often price below real cost because nobody did the math on their hours.

ideas.title: True cost pricing
ideas.text: Works out the cost of each piece including materials, hours and fees, then suggests wholesale and retail prices that leave a margin.

ideas.title: Listing writer
ideas.text: Writes marketplace titles, tags and descriptions that match how buyers search, from photos of the piece.

ideas.title: Order fulfillment
ideas.text: Prints labels, buys postage, sends tracking, and drafts responses to where-is-my-order messages.

ideas.title: Wholesale accounts
ideas.text: Builds line sheets, pitches stores that fit, manages reorders and wholesale minimums.

ideas.title: Market and fair applications
ideas.text: Finds craft fairs that fit your price point, drafts applications with booth photos, and plans stock from past fair sales.

ideas.title: Sales tax
ideas.text: Tracks where you collect sales tax yourself versus where the marketplace does, and files on time.

ideas.title: Custom orders
ideas.text: Handles custom requests: options, deposit, approval of a sketch, and a realistic ship date.

ideas.title: Batch planning
ideas.text: Groups orders into production batches by technique and material so you make twenty rings in one session.

types.name: Tattoo artists
types.who: Shop artists and private studio owners booking custom work and flash.
types.firstHire: A booking and deposit agent. DMs are the front desk, and they never close.

ideas.title: Inquiry sorting
ideas.text: Reads requests with placement, size and reference images, routes the ones that fit your style, and declines the rest kindly.

ideas.title: Deposits and no-shows
ideas.text: Collects deposits on booking, applies the no-show policy, and fills a canceled slot from the waitlist.

ideas.title: Design brief
ideas.text: Turns a client's messy description and ten reference images into a brief you can draw from.

ideas.title: Consent and aftercare
ideas.text: Collects consent forms and ID before the session, sends aftercare by text, and asks for a healed photo at six weeks.

ideas.title: Books open and flash
ideas.text: Plans when to open books and flash days, writes the posts and handles the rush of messages that follow.

ideas.title: Guest spots
ideas.text: Arranges guest spots in other cities: the shop agreement, local license, travel and an announcement to clients there.

ideas.title: Healed portfolio
ideas.text: Builds your portfolio from healed photos, which convince clients more than fresh ones.

ideas.title: Hand and back care
ideas.text: Tracks hours tattooing per week and keeps rest days on the calendar when the books are full.

types.name: Actors, dancers & performers
types.who: Stage and screen actors, voice actors, dancers and choreographers.
types.firstHire: An audition manager. Finding and submitting for the right roles is a part-time job on top of the actual job.

ideas.title: Breakdown scanner
ideas.text: Reads casting breakdowns on Backstage and Actors Access, filters by type, location and union status, and submits for the right ones.

ideas.title: Self-tape logistics
ideas.text: Gets the sides, books a reader, sets up the deadline and checks the tape meets the casting office's specs.

ideas.title: Union earnings
ideas.text: Tracks residuals and earnings toward health plan eligibility thresholds, and flags missing residual payments.

ideas.title: Rep communication
ideas.text: Keeps your agent and manager updated on availability, bookings and conflicts in one weekly note.

ideas.title: Materials refresh
ideas.text: Tells you when headshots, reel and resume are out of date and books the photographer or editor.

ideas.title: Survival job schedule
ideas.text: Fits day-job shifts around auditions and callbacks and swaps shifts when a booking lands.

ideas.title: Choreography rights
ideas.text: For choreographers: licensing terms and credit for work used in videos, tours and competitions.

ideas.title: Training plan
ideas.text: Schedules classes, coaching and conditioning around rehearsal and show schedules.

types.name: Music & arts educators
types.who: Private teachers, online course creators and mentorship programs teaching an instrument or an art.
types.firstHire: A student success agent. Retention decides the business, and students drift away quietly.

ideas.title: Lesson scheduling
ideas.text: Books lessons, handles reschedules and makeups by policy, and keeps every calendar right across time zones.

ideas.title: Practice follow-up
ideas.text: Notices a student who stopped practicing and sends the teacher a heads-up with a suggested message.

ideas.title: Progress reports
ideas.text: Writes each student's progress summary from lesson notes, recordings and practice logs.

ideas.title: Enrollment pipeline
ideas.text: Answers prospects, books trial lessons, follows up after trials and tracks who enrolled.

ideas.title: Failed payments
ideas.text: Retries failed charges, sends a polite card-update request, and tells you before access is cut off.

ideas.title: Student support inbox
ideas.text: Answers questions about schedules, materials and billing, and passes anything about learning to the teacher.

ideas.title: Recital logistics
ideas.text: Plans recitals and showcases: venue, program order, accompanist, rehearsal schedule and family invitations.

ideas.title: Curriculum library
ideas.text: Organizes lesson materials and exercises by level so the right next exercise is always at hand.
